# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 6

---

6:1 Listen therefore, O kings, and understand; take heed, you judges of the ends of the earth.

6:2 Pay attention, you who hold authority over multitudes and take pride in the numbers of your nations.

6:3 For your authority was given to you by the Lord, and your sovereignty belongs to the Most High, who will examine your works and scrutinize your counsels.

6:4 Because as servants of his kingdom you did not judge correctly, nor keep the law, nor walk in accordance with the purpose of God,

6:5 he will come upon you swiftly and terribly; for strict judgment is reserved for those who stand in high places.

6:6 For the lowliest person may be pardoned through mercy, but the mighty will be mightily called to account.

6:7 For the Lord of all is not impressed by anyone's person and does not stand in awe of greatness; for he himself made both small and great alike, and provides equally for all;

6:8 but a rigorous scrutiny awaits those who exercise power.

6:9 It is to you, therefore, O rulers, that my words are addressed, so that you may learn wisdom and not transgress.

6:10 For those who have guarded holy things in a holy manner will themselves be made holy, and those who have received instruction in them will find a defense ready.

6:11 Set your desire on my words, long for them, and you will be instructed.

6:12 Wisdom is radiant and unfading, and she is readily perceived by those who love her, and found by those who seek her.

6:13 She is eager to make herself known to those who desire her.

6:14 One who rises early to seek her will have no trouble, for he will find her seated at his very gate.

6:15 For to direct one's thought toward her is perfect understanding, and one who keeps vigil on her account will soon be free from care;

6:16 for she herself goes about seeking those who are worthy of her, and she meets them graciously on their paths, and in every thought she comes to them.

6:17 For the beginning of wisdom is the genuine desire for instruction, and care for instruction is love of her,

6:18 and love of her is the observance of her laws, and attention to her laws is the guarantee of imperishability,

6:19 and imperishability brings a person near to God;

6:20 so then the desire for wisdom leads to a kingdom.

6:21 Therefore if you delight in thrones and scepters, O rulers of the peoples, honor wisdom, that you may reign for ever.

6:22 What wisdom is and how she came to be I will declare to you, and I will not conceal the mysteries from you; but I will trace her from the very beginning of creation, I will make knowledge of her plain to see, and I will not pass by the truth.

6:23 Nor will I make my way with consuming envy, for envy has no fellowship with wisdom.

6:24 A multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world, and a prudent king is the stability of his people.

6:25 Therefore be instructed by my words, and it will be to your profit.

---

## Council Notes

**On 6:6 — "tested" vs. "called to account":** EMET "mightily tested," LOGOS "mightily called to account," PNEUMA "powerful reckoning." SOPHIA adopts "called to account" — exetasthēsontai means to be examined/investigated; "tested" (EMET) leans moral; "called to account" has the judicial quality the context demands.

**On 6:12 — "radiant" vs. "luminous":** EMET/LOGOS "radiant," PNEUMA "luminous." SOPHIA retains "radiant" — lampra is the base form of the word for brilliance/brightness; "radiant" is slightly warmer and more appropriate to the female personification.

**On 6:15 — "perfect understanding" vs. "perfect prudence":** EMET "perfect understanding," LOGOS "perfect understanding," PNEUMA "perfect understanding." All agents agree — phronēsis here means practical wisdom/understanding; no disagreement.

**On 6:17–20 — the sorites:** SOPHIA preserves the chain-link structure of LOGOS. Each step is one verse; the logical progression must be visible: desire → love → observance → imperishability → nearness to God → kingdom. PNEUMA's short-step version is effective for readability but breaks the literary form.

**On 6:23 — phthonos/envy:** LOGOS "consuming envy," EMET "sickly envy," PNEUMA "twisted by envy." SOPHIA adopts LOGOS "consuming envy" — phthonos carries the sense of wasting/consuming; the connection to 2:24 (the devil's phthonos) is an intentional authorial echo.

**On 6:24 — "salvation of the world" vs. "welfare of the world":** EMET "salvation," LOGOS "welfare," PNEUMA "flourishing." SOPHIA adopts "welfare" — sōtēria here means the world's well-being/safety/preservation, not theological salvation; context is political-philosophical.
